title: Pichia-CLM improves recombinant protein expression in Komagataella phaffii
summary: A GRU encoder-decoder language model learns host-specific amino-acid-to-codon patterns and designs synonymous sequences. Across six proteins, the study reports the best titer for five against four commercial optimization tools; human serum albumin reached about threefold the native-sequence titer. Results are plate-scale expression measurements, not manufacturing economics or clinical product outcomes.

evidence.tested: The source reports the study-specific result summarized here.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader deployment or clinical benefit are not established by this source review.
evidence.ai_role: The learned host codon language model generates optimized coding sequences; researchers experimentally compare protein titers with native sequences and four commercial tools.
